name: MCP3424 18-bit 4-channel ADC (I2C)
description: Microchip 18-bit delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter with 4 differential inputs (±2.048 V full scale, PGA x1/x2/x4/x8), on-board 2.048 V reference and an I2C interface; 12/14/16/18-bit at 240/60/15/3.75 samples per second. Runs on 2.7-5.5 V. Sold as: DFRobot Fermion MCP3424 18-Bit ADC module (DFR0316), two 6-pin headers (GND, +5V, C3+, C3-, C4+, C4- and SCL, SDA, C2-, C2+, C1-, C1+), I2C address 0x68 with both DIP switches off (0x6A, 0x6C, 0x6E).
eli5: Gives your board four very precise voltage inputs that can even measure tiny or negative voltages, and sends the numbers over I2C.

pins.name: +5V
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-5.5 V. Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico: the board's 1 kΩ I2C pull-ups go to this pin

pins.name: C3+
pins.description: Channel 3 positive input (CH3+); reads C3+ minus C3-, ±2.048 V at gain 1; keep it between GND and the supply

pins.name: C3-
pins.description: Channel 3 negative input (CH3-); keep it between GND and the supply. Tie C3- to GND for single-ended use

pins.name: C4+
pins.description: Channel 4 positive input (CH4+); reads C4+ minus C4-, ±2.048 V at gain 1; keep it between GND and the supply

pins.name: C4-
pins.description: Channel 4 negative input (CH4-); keep it between GND and the supply. Tie C4- to GND for single-ended use

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (1 kΩ pull-up to +5V on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (1 kΩ pull-up to +5V on the board)

pins.name: C2-
pins.description: Channel 2 negative input (CH2-); keep it between GND and the supply. Tie C2- to GND for single-ended use

pins.name: C2+
pins.description: Channel 2 positive input (CH2+); reads C2+ minus C2-, ±2.048 V at gain 1; keep it between GND and the supply

pins.name: C1-
pins.description: Channel 1 negative input (CH1-); keep it between GND and the supply. Tie C1- to GND for single-ended use

pins.name: C1+
pins.description: Channel 1 positive input (CH1+); reads C1+ minus C1-, ±2.048 V at gain 1; keep it between GND and the supply

buildNotes: Power the board from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico: its 1 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to the +5V pin, so 5 V there would put 5 V on the GPIOs.
Each reading is C+ minus C-. For a single-ended voltage, tie that channel's C- to GND; you then get 0 to +2.048 V (gain 1). Every input pin must stay between GND - 0.3 V and the supply + 0.3 V.

One-shot conversion: write one configuration byte 0x80 | (channel-1) << 5 | rate << 2 | gain, wait (267 ms at 18 bits), read 3 data bytes + config byte (2 + 1 below 18 bits) and accept it when bit 7 (RDY) of the config byte is 0.
Volts = code x 2.048 V / 2^(N-1) / PGA: 15.625 µV per code at 18 bits, 62.5 µV at 16 bits, 250 µV at 14 bits, 1 mV at 12 bits (gain 1). Codes are two's complement.
Address: DIP switch A drives Adr0, B drives Adr1 (off = pulled low): A off B off 0x68, A off B on 0x6A, A on B off 0x6C, both on 0x6E.
Above about ±2.048 V / gain the code saturates at 131071 or -131072 (18 bits): lower the gain or divide the voltage down.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mcp3424 import MCP3424

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
adc = MCP3424(i2c, addr=0x68, bits=18, gain=1)  # DIP switches A and B off
while True:
    r1 = adc.read_raw(1)
    r3 = adc.read_raw(3)
    print('CH1=%d %.5fV CH3=%d %.5fV' % (r1, r1 * adc.lsb(), r3, r3 * adc.lsb()))
    time.sleep(1)
